- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (sentiment > 0.67) and understate when bearish (sentiment < 0.33), especially in early forecast periods.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment was high and price surged recently.
- Underreact to sustained bullish sentiment; if sentiment remains > 0.67 for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast mean by 2–5% to avoid mean reversion lag.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), forecasts often lag behind true price; adjust by adding 1–3% to forecast for the next 3–5 days if sentiment is holding steady.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope to prevent over-optimism.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), forecast should be smoother; apply low-pass filter or dampen volatility in 30d forecast to avoid erratic peaks.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true price exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust future forecasts downward by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion bias.
